title: TTFB and frontend performance budgets
description: Learn about TTFB and frontend performance budgets. Master the concepts, patterns, and best practices.

data.text: Time to First Byte (TTFB) and performance budgets are foundational concepts for frontend performance engineering. TTFB measures server responsiveness, while performance budgets provide systematic constraints to maintain fast, reliable user experiences.

TTFB measures the time between the browser requesting a page and receiving the first byte of data from the server. It includes DNS lookup, TCP connection, TLS negotiation, and server processing time. A good TTFB is under 200 milliseconds.

data.title: Measuring TTFB
data.content: Use Performance API to measure TTFB in production.

items: Use CDN to reduce network latency and DNS lookup time
Implement HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 for faster connection establishment
Optimize server-side code and database queries
Use server-side caching (Redis, Memcached) for fast responses
Enable compression (gzip, Brotli) to reduce transfer time
Preconnect to important origins to speed up connection setup

data.text: Performance budgets are systematic limits on the size and complexity of your web resources. They prevent performance regressions by ensuring that new features don't make your site slower. Budgets can be set for JavaScript bundles, CSS files, images, and total page weight.

data.title: Performance Budget Configuration
data.content: Set up performance budgets using webpack-bundle-analyzer.

items: **Size Budgets**: Maximum file sizes for JS, CSS, images, fonts
**Quantity Budgets**: Maximum number of requests or resources
**Rule Budgets**: Limits on specific performance patterns (no layout shifts)

data.text: Start by measuring your current performance, then set budgets slightly below your current metrics to drive improvement. Consider your target users' network conditions and devices when setting budgets.

data.title: Budget Calculation Example
data.content: Calculate performance budgets based on target metrics.

data.text: Integrate performance budget checks into your CI/CD pipeline to catch regressions before deployment. Use tools like Lighthouse CI, webpack performance hints, or custom scripts.

data.title: CI/CD Performance Budget Check
data.content: Add performance budget checks to your build process.

data.title: Budget Enforcement
data.text: Performance budgets should be enforced in CI/CD but allow temporary overrides for critical features. Balance user experience with business needs.
Continuously monitor your performance budgets in production using real user monitoring (RUM). Set up alerts when budgets are exceeded to catch regressions quickly.

terms.definition: The time between a browser's request and the first byte of response received from the server.
Systematic limits on resource sizes and complexity to prevent performance regressions.
Performance monitoring based on actual user data rather than synthetic tests.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: TTFB measures server responsiveness, aim for under 200ms
Optimize TTFB with CDNs, HTTP/2, server caching, and compression
Performance budgets prevent regressions by limiting resource sizes
Set budgets based on current metrics and target user conditions
Enforce budgets in CI/CD to catch issues before deployment
Monitor budgets in production with real user monitoring
data.takeaway: TTFB and performance budgets provide the foundation for systematic performance optimization and regression prevention.
